chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Release and sales of the Decca 78 albums
summary: The producer Perez had pre-sold 25-30 thousand copies in Latin America; albums of eight sides sold for about four dollars.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay. Now those recordings they came out at 78 RPM.
Right.
How soon after were they released? Were they released altogether or were they done over a period of time?

No, in those days they don't take as much time that the regular American company take, in account that Perez, and he was the producer of those records, he was Spanish, he had sold practically twenty-five or thirty thousand copies before we recorded, in South and Central America, so it was a sure thing. It's not like now that you got to play it over the radio to make it popular.
I see.
They were sold before we record it.
Why was that, because of his name, Miguelito Valdes' name?
Baeause of his name and because of the quality of the recording that we made in the United States.
Okay. There were twenty six different tunes, were they released all at one time or did they release a few at a time?
No, a few at a time. Let'sssay we then made an album, two albums.....
Eight in an album, eight sides?

Yes. So they made the first album. The first album was a hot cake so they - in those days they were afraid that one album kill the other one because they were so well accepted that the people don't mind to buy this one and the next one. They was, no, that's too old, no they was buying the first one and the second one and the third one. You know...
They really sold, eh?
Yes, yes.
They sold the 78 RPM set first, right?
Right.
Ahh - What did an album cost, let's see, eight -sides- four records each side?
They cost about four dollars, four fifty.
Four dollars, so it was about a dollar per 78 then, right?
Right.
